chapters.title: How lonely sits the city
chapters.summary: An alphabet poem mourning Jerusalem after its fall, a widow with none to comfort her. Is it nothing to you, all you who pass by?

chapters.title: The Lord as enemy
chapters.summary: The poet describes God's anger destroying Zion and grieves the starving children, urging the people to pour out their hearts like water.

chapters.title: His mercies are new every morning
chapters.summary: A man who has seen affliction remembers God's faithfulness: His compassions fail not; they are new every morning. The Lord is good to those who wait for Him.

chapters.title: The gold has dimmed
chapters.summary: The horrors of the siege are recalled: famine, shame and the failure of prophets and priests. Yet Zion's punishment will end.

chapters.title: Restore us to yourself
chapters.summary: A final prayer: remember us, Lord. You reign forever. Turn us back to You, O Lord, and we shall be turned.
